title: `resource_link`
description: A tool result block that points at a resource URI instead of inlining its contents.
question: Does a resource link reach the agent as a reference it can follow?
notes: Both adapters that reach 2026-07-28 deliver the URI but neither keeps the link as a structured reference; 3 cannot reach the revision.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI 1.15.1 requires MCP Python SDK 1.26.x, so it cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.
notes_by_num.2: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2 requires mcp<2.0.0, so it cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.
notes_by_num.3: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.22.0: the link is re-serialized as JSON inside a text item, retaining `uri`, `name` and `description`. Followable, but only after parsing text.
notes_by_num.4: Pydantic AI 2.40.0: only the URI is returned, as a bare string. The link is still followable, but its `name`, `description` and `mimeType` are gone.
notes_by_num.5: Mastra 1.17.3 negotiated MCP 2025-11-25. The scanner refused to compare that capture with a 2026-07-28 source.

verdict.headline: The URI survives in both, the structure in neither.
verdict.detail: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.22.0 preserves the whole link inside JSON text; Pydantic AI 2.40.0 reduces it to the bare URI. An agent can still follow the reference in both cases, which is why this is a change rather than a loss. CrewAI, LangChain and Mastra cannot negotiate MCP 2026-07-28, so they reach none of it.

usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: Resource links are how a large result stays out of the context window until something asks for it. A framework that flattens the link to text keeps the URI as prose and loses the ability to fetch what it points at.
